pr_title: net: Change the net_linkaddr struct to not use pointers
pr_body:
Previously the net_linkaddr struct had pointers to the link address. This is error prone and difficult to handle if cloning the packet as those pointers can point to wrong place. Mitigate this issue by allocating the space for link address in net_linkaddr struct. This will increase the size of the net_pkt by 4 bytes for IEEE 802.15.4 where the link address length is 8, but there no increase in size if link address is 6 bytes like in Ethernet/Wi-Fi.

Fixes #86652

issue_context.title: net: ip: Link Layer Address of DGRAM packets received by sockets might be corrupted
issue_context.body:
<!--
**Notes**
Github Discussions (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/discussions)
are available to first verify that the issue is a genuine Zephyr bug and not a
consequence of Zephyr services misuse.

This issue list is only for bugs in the main Zephyr code base
(https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/). If the bug is for a project
fork (such as NCS) specific feature, please open an issue in the fork project
instead.
-->

**Describe the bug**
<!--
A clear and concise description of what the bug is.

Please also mention any information which could help others to understand
the problem you're facing:
 - What target platform are you using?
 - What have you tried to diagnose or workaround this issue?
 - Is this a regression? If yes, have you been able to "git bisect" it to a
   specific commit?
 - ...
-->


While our Wi-Fi STA with hostap is running zperf download Peak Throughput test, when AP starts group rekey process,
it sends EAPOL M1 packet to us and expects M2 packet. But hostap receives a packet with wrong link address. (It should be AP's mac address. But it is mac address of zperf client device like PC backend)
The root cause is that struct `net_linkaddr lladdr_src->addr` in `struct net_pkt` is a pointer rather than local storage.
It is assigned in `ethernet_recv()`, pointing to payload L2 header of EAPOL pkt. But then the L2 header is removed in payload after l2_processed. (`net_pkt_set_l2_processed(1)` in `process_data()`)
Then for the `AF_PACKET` family, the EAPOL pkt goes through
`net_packet_socket_input()->net_packet_socket_input()->net_conn_input()->conn_raw_socket()`.
In `conn_raw_socket()` it is cloned. And the cloned pkt will be sent to sockets' `recv_q`. The original pkt will be freed.
But during the pkt clone in `clone_pkt_attributes()`, `clone_pkt->lladdr_src->addr` is directly value set by
`orig_pkt->lladdr_src->addr`, which points to original buffer, which will be freed and override.
(There is `clone_pkt_lladdr()` trying to fix this issue. But it only fixes the RAW socket issue. Because DGRAM socket packet is cloned after L2 processed, which means it does not have L2 header. And `lladdr_src`, at least in Wi-Fi case, points to L2 header of pkt payload. So for DGRAM packet, `clone_pkt_lladdr()` cannot find offset for lladdr and it will remain pointing to original pkt payload)

Simple example for DGRAM AF_PACKET helping to understand
`orig_pkt->lladdr_src->addr`  Pointing to  `orig_pkt->buffer->data => net_pkt_pull(orig_pkt, L2_hdr size) =>
clone_pkt->lladdr_src->addr` Pointing to `orig_pkt->buffer->data => clone_pkt_lladdr() => net_pkt_find_offset(orig_pkt->lladdr_src->addr)` fail because pkt's L2_hdr is removed


**To Reproduce**
<!--
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. mkdir build; cd build
2. cmake -DBOARD=board\_xyz
3. make
4. See error
-->
1. Build Wi-Fi STA example with hostap.
2. Set external AP's group rekey period to 10 seconds.
3. Do wifi connect with external AP.
4. Do zperf download peak throughput test longer than AP's group rekey period.
We will disconnect after when AP wants to do group rekey.

**Expected behavior**
<!--
A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.
-->
We do rekey and zperf download continuously.

**Impact**
<!--
What impact does this issue have on your progress (e.g., annoyance, showstopper)
-->
Wi-Fi is disconnected.
Besides, there is risk of corrupted link layer address on all AF_PACKET DGRAM packets

**Logs and console output**
<!--
If applicable, add console logs or other types of debug information
e.g Wireshark capture or Logic analyzer capture (upload in zip archive).
copy-and-paste text and put a code fence (\`\`\`) before and after, to help
explain the issue. (if unable to obtain text log, add a screenshot)
-->
```
<dbg> wpa_supp: wpa_printf_impl: ml: Not associated - Delay processing of received EAPOL frame (state=COMPLETED bssid=xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx)
<inf> wpa_supp: ml: CTRL-EVENT-DISCONNECTED
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
-OS: Linux
-Toolchain: Zephyr SDK
-Version: Zephyr 4.0

**Additional context**

target configuration, ...
-->
